commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix: keep consecutive text-only replies in separate bubbles
commits.body:
#40 groups consecutive assistant messages into one run so an action group split
across a message boundary renders as a single summary row. The fallback formed a
run whenever the buffer held more than one message, including when nothing in it
was groupable, which merged two unrelated replies into one bubble.

Visible on OMP while a queued prompt runs: the live order is user, user,
assistant, assistant, so both answers shared a bubble with no way to tell which
prompt each belonged to. Reopening the session split them again, because OMP's
persisted history is strictly interleaved, so the same conversation rendered two
different ways. OMP only ever produces text parts, so a run should never have
formed for it at all.

A run now forms only when the buffered messages actually contain a reasoning,
tool or patch part.

commits.subject: fix: repair what the PI merge dropped
commits.body:
#42 merged main into its branch and resolved three conflicts by keeping its own
side, which silently reverted work that had landed in between:

- `type Translator` disappeared, so the web build failed with a dozen TS2304
  errors. The regression suites still passed, because they assert against source
  text and never compile — worth remembering about that style of test.
- The SSE heartbeat was gone, which reintroduces the 30s reconnect loop #38
  fixed. The heartbeat test caught it by timing out.
- The session card's Open button came back, along with a `PlayIcon` reference
  whose import no longer exists. It was removed on purpose in #40 as redundant
  with the card itself being clickable.

Verified after the repair against real OMP 17.1.3: health reports the backend,
an idle event stream emits `: ping`, and a prompt round-trips. `--backend pi`
resolves to `npx.cmd -y @victor-software-house/pi-acp` on Windows; the adapter
itself is not exercised here because it is not installed on this machine.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(bridge): survive a cold adapter start and say why one died
commits.body:
Both problems hit on the first real attempt to reach PI through the adapter.

An adapter launched with `npx` downloads itself on first use. The 10s handshake
timeout expired while npm was still fetching, so the first PI connection always
failed with "request timed out: initialize" and the second succeeded — a
first-run failure every user would meet. The handshake now allows 90s.

The adapter then exited 1 and the app was told only "ACP adapter exited (1)",
while the reason sat on stderr: the adapter requires Bun, which was missing. The
exit error now carries a short stderr tail, so a missing prerequisite is visible
where it is read. Several lines are kept because a Windows shell error wraps the
useful part away from the sentence that follows it.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat: run PI on Node, and let its tool calls through
commits.body:
PI support shipped against @victor-software-house/pi-acp, which declares
engines.bun and shells out to `bun`. This project runs on Node everywhere, so
the default adapter is now @automatalabs/pi-acp, which embeds PI through its
published SDK and needs only Node 22.19. PI itself was never the problem — it
is an npm package that runs on Node; only that adapter was.

The version is pinned. An unpinned default failed with `notarget` when 0.2.6
appeared in the registry index before its tarball could be fetched, so a
floating default breaks whenever an upstream publish goes wrong.

Two defects surfaced only once a real PI answered, both invisible with OMP:

- Tool calls never ran. PI's adapter asks permission before each one and the
  bridge refused every agent-initiated request as unimplemented, so a prompt to
  write a file reported success and wrote nothing. Permission requests are now
  granted with the broadest allow option offered, which matches OMP, whose agent
  approves its own tool calls without asking. Verified: the file is created.
- A reply arrived as one message per token. PI streams chunks with no messageId,
  and minting an id per chunk split "PI_NODE_OK" into four messages. Chunks
  without an id now append to the message the same role opened in that turn,
  scoped to the turn so a later reply cannot land on an earlier one. Replay is
  excluded, where a missing id means separate persisted messages.

Authentication also preferred the adapter's first method, an env-var Anthropic
key that is usually unset, over its stored PI credentials. Non-env-var methods
now win, so the bridge uses the credentials the harness already has.

Both defects were first found and fixed in #43; this is the smaller change that
unblocks PI on Node, and that PR's profile architecture still stands on its own.

Verified against PI 0.82.1 and adapter 0.2.5: session create, streamed prompt as
a single message, a tool call that writes the file, model list, session list, and
abort. OMP 17.1.3 re-checked for regressions. Bridge 32/32, web 6/6.
